messages:
Maya Patel: [incident bot] paging: High KV cache evictions observed on prod-gpu-3 at 21:07 UTC, cont-batch latency spike. Investigating.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2109876543. Priority: P1. Assigned: oncall eng-sre.
Samira Khan: seeing increased OOMs on g4 instances, eviction rate ~x6 over baseline. Paging to NVMe at ~80MB/s. :rotating_light: 
Li Chen: can you paste logs? particularly eviction trace and which model variants are active
Samira Khan: logs clipped:
```
[evict] ts=21:06:45 model=awq-3b quant=int8 kv_size=184M active_batches=48
[evict] ts=21:06:46 model=gptq-6b quant=awq kv_size=312M active_batches=52
[batch] dropped=12 reason=kv-pressure
```
Samira Khan: noticed config changed at 20:55 — cont-batch max_batch=64 -> 128 via rollout
Dave Ortiz: @Samira can you confirm if rollout was the dedicated pool? I think this was a global rollout
Anita Gomez: I rolled a tuning change to cont-batch across prod yesterday (understand the risk). It increased max_batch to 128 for medium latency customers to gain throughput.
Maya Patel: that aligns. We might be seeing combinatorial effect: quant path (int8/awq) increases kv footprint and higher batch sizes magnify per-request KV allocation -> spill
Li Chen: kernel selection logs show fallback to slower kernels for awq on a subset -> increases memory per key
Samira Khan: mitigation idea: revert cont-batch max back to 64 for prod-gpu pools + pin model variants to gptq fallback where kv footprint lower
Maya Patel: agree. Plan:
1) rollback cont-batch max_batch -> 64 (targeted to prod-gpu-* pools) — Samira
2) pin models awq-3b -> awq-3b-lowkvc (if available) / or gptq-6b for high-throughput routes — Li
3) raise eviction throttle and enable early batching backpressure — Dave
4) customer comms and impact assessment — Anita
Samira Khan: starting rollback now. Running deploy: `sh /ops/rollback-contbatch.sh --pool prod-gpu-* --batch 64`
deploy-bot: Rollback queued: job id 4587. ETA ~45s.
Samira Khan: rollback done on prod-gpu-1..3. Monitoring eviction rate.
Samira Khan: eviction rate back to ~1.2x baseline. latency 95p down from 2.8s -> 1.1s
Li Chen: pinned awq models to low-kv variant for canary routes. Still evaluating kernel fallback heatmap.
Dave Ortiz: enabled eviction throttle at 60% and reduced continuous batching window from 250ms -> 120ms
Maya Patel: assessing customer impact: a handful of customers experienced elevated latency >5s for 12m window, no error rate increase, some tail token drops but no data loss. Anita please draft severity summary
Anita Gomez: working on severity: P1 (service degradation), impacted customer count: ~7 customers (accounts with heavy long-context workloads), ETA for follow-up: 1h for post-mortem
Samira Khan: follow-up: we saw KV size per-request drop after rollbacks by ~40MB average for awq-3b paths
Li Chen: action items:
- short term: revert cont-batch (done), pin model variants (in progress), enable throttle (done)
- medium: add model-quant-kv profiler to CI to catch these regressions
- long term: make kernel selection deterministic per-variant + warn when estimated kv footprint > threshold
Maya Patel: thanks team. I'll hand off to oncall for post-incident tracking. Add timeline and changelog to INC-2026-2109876543
oncall-bot: Handing off to engineering oncall: Samira Khan
Dave Ortiz: adding notes to the incident doc: `/incidents/INC-2026-2109876543` — include config diffs
Samira Khan: will follow-up with postmortem within 24h. quick note: correlate batch size rollout with quant-path kernel fallback in CI
Anita Gomez: customer comms draft ready, pinging legal for sensitive wording. :email:
Maya Patel: closing loop — move to postmortem once doc is populated. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
